subject: Per-route economics handoff & dashboard permissions
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Per-route economics handoff & dashboard permissions

Team —

Quick request from the Acme renewal/expansion thread: Priya asked for a per-route breakdown of cost and p99 latency that they can attach to their internal FinOps review next week. They need two concrete things from us:

1) A dashboard or export that shows, per-route (endpoint) for their tenant (acme-prod and acme-staging): token cost by day, average token cost per request, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and per-model inference unit used.
2) A permissions/delegation matrix so Acme can give their internal FinOps read-only access without exposing internal debugging traces.

Constraints I heard in the discovery call: needs prod/staging split, 30-day rolling window, and a CSV export. Priya is cc'd if she wants to correct me on scope.

Can we align on who owns the delivery (console wiring, sampling/query performance, export format) and a realistic timeline? If possible I'd like a small scoped deliverable for the renewal meeting on 24 Jun (7 business days).

Attachment: per-route-requirements.pdf (one-pager from Acme)

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-route economics handoff & dashboard permissions

Jonas —

Thanks for the context. A few clarifying Qs from the console/instrumentation side so we scope appropriately:

- Aggregation window: do they need daily rollups only, or also hourly for the last 48 hours? Hourly increases query cost especially across many routes.
- Sampling: for p99 latency and tail cost we usually sample full traces for heavy routes and estimate for low-volume routes. Do they accept sampled p99 + confidence intervals?
- Models: do they want breakdown by model version (e.g., gptx-20b-v1) or just model family?

If they need full fidelity (hourly + exact p99 across all routes), delivery will be longer. I can sketch a lightweight dashboard with daily rollups and CSV export by EOD Tue if that works.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Product Manager, Console

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

All —

Leaving the technical nitty-gritty to Camila & Markus, but on the product/permissions side here's my proposed owner matrix and timeline:

- Product (console UX + export): Camila (deliver wireframe + CSV schema) — target: 2027-06-15

I created a starter sheet and attached a delegation matrix for review. If we agree on the scope above we can get the quick export and a read-only view ready.

From: Priya Shah <priya@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-route economics handoff & dashboard permissions

Thanks everyone — helpful. A few clarifications from Acme's side:

- We do need prod/staging split (explicit columns).
- Hourly is only required for the last 48 hours to debug spikes; daily rollups for the 30-day window are fine for FinOps reporting.
- Read-only view should be SSO-mapped to our Okta groups (FinOps_ReadOnly). We can share role IDs.

One ask: can you also include a simple per-route expected cost-per-1k-requests (to make it easier for our budget owners to reason)? If that can be calculated from tokens & cost columns that should be fine.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Priya Shah
Senior Cloud Finance Manager
Acme Analytics

Camila / Grace —

Quick tech note on sampling & p99: for low-volume routes (<100 req/day) computing exact p99 from raw traces is noisy; we should either
- advertise sampled p99 with a 95% confidence interval for routes <1k/day, or
- fall back to estimated tail using model_family-level histograms.

I'll add a column "p99_estimate_flag" to the export so FinOps knows which rows are sampled/estimated. Also adding an extra column for "cost_per_1k_requests_usd" derived from tokens and cost_usd.

Attachment: sample-api-query.txt (example SQL-like query for the export)
